title: How to Slice Beets Thinly for Elegant Salad Garnish
meta_description: Learn how to slice beets thin for stunning salads. Master the mandoline for restaurant-quality, paper-thin beet rounds and garnishes every time.
html:
There is something about paper-thin beet slices that transforms a basic garden salad into a restaurant-quality dish. Whether you are working with earthy red beets, golden beets, or the vibrant stripes of Chioggia, the goal is a translucent slice that curls elegantly on the plate and absorbs vinaigrettes quickly.

While a sharp chef's knife works for basic chunks, trying to get a consistent, sheer slice by hand is tedious and often uneven. To truly master this technique, you need to slice beets thin mandoline style. Using a dedicated slicer ensures that every piece is the exact same thickness, which is the secret to a professional presentation and a uniform texture in every bite.

Preparing Your Beets for Slicing

Before you reach for your equipment, you have to decide between raw and cooked beets. For a crisp, refreshing crunch, raw beets are the way to go. For a softer, more mellow flavor, boil or roast them first. If you are slicing cooked beets, let them cool completely in the refrigerator; warm beets are too soft and will mash rather than slice.

Scrub your beets thoroughly under cold water to remove any grit. If you are using raw beets, trim the greens and the root end to create a flat surface. This stability is crucial when using a slicer, as a rolling beet is a safety hazard. If the beet is oddly shaped, slice a small sliver off one side to create a steady base.

How to Slice Beets Thin Mandoline Style

Once your beets are prepped, it's time to set up your station. To get those elegant, translucent rounds, you want a setting between 1/16th of an inch and 1/8th of an inch. Using a Mandoline Slicer allows you to dial in this exact thickness, ensuring you don't end up with some slices that are thick and woody and others that are practically invisible.

Place the Mandoline Slicer on a non-slip mat or a damp paper towel to keep it from sliding on your counter. Secure your beet firmly against the feeding tray. As you glide the vegetable across the blade, use a steady, rhythmic motion. Don't force the beet; let the razor-sharp blade do the work.

Prioritizing Safety with Hand Guards

Anyone who has spent time in a professional kitchen knows that mandolines are efficient but unforgiving. The blades are designed to cut through dense root vegetables with zero resistance, which means they will cut through a fingertip just as easily.

Never slide the beet by hand as you reach the end of the vegetable. This is where the hand guard becomes non-negotiable. The Mandoline Slicer comes equipped with adjustable hand guards that act as a physical barrier between your skin and the blade. Always lock the guard onto the beet and use it to push the vegetable through to the very last sliver.

Creative Ways to Use Your Thin Beet Slices

Now that you have a pile of perfectly uniform slices, you can use them for more than just a basic side salad. Here are a few ways to elevate your plating:

  • Beet Carpaccio: Arrange raw, paper-thin slices in an overlapping circle on a platter. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, flaky sea salt, and topped with capers.
  • Pickled Garnishes: Quickly pickle your slices in a mixture of apple cider vinegar, sugar, and salt for 30 minutes. They turn a brilliant magenta and add a tangy pop to tacos or burgers.
  • The Salad Ribbon: Instead of rounds, turn the beet 90 degrees and slice lengthwise to create long, elegant ribbons. Curl these into small nests on top of arugula.
  • Layered Tartlets: Use the slices to create a shingled pattern on top of a goat cheese tart before baking.

Cleaning and Maintenance Tips

Beets are notorious for staining everything they touch. To prevent your equipment from becoming permanently pink, rinse your Mandoline Slicer immediately after use. Run warm, soapy water through the blades and use a soft brush to clear any small fibers trapped in the adjustable settings.

Avoid using abrasive steel wool on the plastic components, as scratches can trap food particles and bacteria. Once clean, dry the blade thoroughly to prevent any oxidation or spotting, ensuring your tool stays sharp for the next meal prep session.

FAQ

Can I slice frozen beets on a mandoline?

No. Frozen or partially frozen beets are too hard and can damage the blade or cause the vegetable to slip, which is dangerous. Always thaw your beets completely and pat them dry before slicing.

Which beet variety is best for thin slicing?

Chioggia beets (the candy-striped variety) are visually stunning when sliced thin, as the rings are clearly visible. However, standard red and golden beets work perfectly for a classic look.

How do I stop my beet slices from bleeding into other salad ingredients?

If you are using raw beets, toss them in a light dressing of oil and acid first. If using cooked beets, pat them dry with a paper towel. To keep a salad pristine, place the beet slices on top of the greens just before serving rather than tossing them in.
